$comment: Golden cases for the filter grammar. Every case evaluates against seed.json at seed.now. 'expect' lists task nums in ascending order; the parser test compares the AST, the store test compares the returned set. Expected values were computed independently of any implementation. Do not edit this file to make a test pass.

grammar.ebnf: query := or_expr ; or_expr := and_expr { '|' and_expr } ; and_expr := term { WS term } ; term := [ '-' ] ( group | predicate | phrase | word ) ; group := '(' or_expr ')' ; predicate := key ':' value | '#' tag | '@' person [ ':' role ] ; phrase := '"' { CHAR } '"' ; word := CHAR { CHAR }
grammar.precedence: '-' binds tightest, then implicit AND (whitespace), then '|'. Parentheses override.
grammar.case: Keys, values, tags, and person handles are case-insensitive. Free text is case-insensitive. Tag and person values preserve their stored case for display.
grammar.whitespace: One or more spaces separate terms. A quoted phrase may contain spaces.
grammar.unknown_key: An unrecognized key:value pair is a parse error, not free text. Error message: `unknown filter key "foo" (try: is, p, due, start, src, has, notify, grp)`.
grammar.date_keyword_rule: A bare weekday name means the next occurrence strictly after today, except when today is that weekday, in which case it means today. Comparison operators are :, :<=, :>=, :<, :>.
grammar.date_comparison: A date-only due value compares by calendar date in seed.timezone. A datetime due value compares by its date component for date predicates.

cases.note: open = status not in (done, dropped). inbox is open.
Literal match. 110 is snoozed but the grammar does not imply view defaults.
Unset priority never matches a p: comparison.
@person with no role matches assigner, assignee, involved, and waiting_on.
grp: matches a direct task-to-group link OR any task involving a member of that group.
Empty result is a valid expectation. Do not treat it as an unimplemented case.
Free text hits FTS5 over title and notes. Prefix matching is on: 'cert' matches 'certs'.
start_at is in the future relative to seed.now.

AND binds tighter than OR, so this parses as (is:open AND #monday) OR #finance. Task 111 is done and carries #finance, and it matches the right side because no is:open guard applies there. If you expected [102, 104, 108] you applied is:open across the whole expression, which is the most common way to get this wrong. See the ast_cases entry for the same string.

This is the home view default, and it is a saved filter rather than special-cased logic. Inbox is excluded here because the top bar carries its count instead. Task 105 is the only inbox item in the seed, so it is the only difference from the same query without -is:inbox.

date_cases.$comment: Date keyword resolution against seed.now (2026-08-03T10:30:00-05:00, a Monday, America/Chicago). Rules were stated in grammar.date_keyword_rule; these fix them to values. Date parsing is the last remaining place in this corpus where a wrong answer looks completely reasonable.
notes: mon resolves to today because today IS Monday. A weekday name means the next occurrence strictly after today ONLY when today is a different weekday. Rolling forward a week here is the common wrong answer.
eow is the Sunday of the current week, so the week starts Monday.
+1m is calendar arithmetic with clamping, not 30 days. From 2026-01-31, +1m is 2026-02-28.
All of these resolve in seed.timezone, not UTC. At 2026-08-03T23:30-05:00 the server clock is already 2026-08-04 in UTC and 'today' is still 2026-08-03.
